You can inspect internal activations during inference by using observability methods that decouple capture from the hot path, so the model keeps serving while internal states are staged asynchronously [7]. One system reports full layer-wise activation trajectories with only 0.4%–6.8% overhead offline and about 6% in online serving, while preserving serving optimizations and GPU memory budgets [7]. Another approach passively observes hidden states and attention patterns, compresses them into fixed-budget descriptors, and predicts outcomes with negligible inference cost [1].

If you want the activations for analysis or control rather than just monitoring, logit-lens and steering-vector tooling can collect layer-wise trajectories and even apply steering without extra forward passes [4]. Other papers use activations to predict importance, uncertainty, or correctness, showing that internal signals can be extracted efficiently for reasoning analysis and early stopping [2, 5, 9].
